plan.title: Alan Turing: The Mind That Shaped Modern Computing
plan.description: A short profile of Alan Turing, the British mathematician who helped break wartime codes and imagined the modern computer. It explains why his ideas still shape the technology we use today.

beats.narration: Can a machine think? Alan Turing asked that question decades before anyone owned a computer. He was a British mathematician, and his answer changed how we live, work and talk to machines.

Turing imagined a simple abstract machine that could follow written instructions. In theory, it could carry out any calculation. That idea became the blueprint for every computer, phone and laptop we use today.

During the Second World War, Turing worked with a team in Britain to break enemy coded messages. Their work helped the Allies, and historians widely credit it with shortening the war and saving many lives.
After the war, he proposed a test for machine intelligence. If you cannot tell a machine from a person in conversation, perhaps it is thinking. People still debate that test today.

props.heading: The Turing test
items: Can you tell which is which?

beats.narration: Turing was treated cruelly by the country he served, and he died young. Yet his ideas live in every device you touch. He taught us to ask what machines could become.

props.text: He taught us to ask what machines could become.
